commands.text:
set +e
npm audit --audit-level=high --json > audit-report.json
AUDIT_EXIT=$?
set -e
node scripts/check-audit-allowlist.mjs audit-report.json .github/audit-allowlist.json "$AUDIT_EXIT"

{
  echo "## CI summary (node ${{ matrix.node-version }})"
  echo ""
  echo "| Step | Result |"
  echo "| --- | --- |"
  echo "| npm audit (high) | ${{ steps.audit.outcome }} |"
  echo "| typecheck / build / test | ${{ job.status }} |"
  echo "| Commit | \`${{ github.sha }}\` |"
} >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"

{
  echo "## Manifest integrity"
  echo ""
  if [ "${{ steps.verify.outcome }}" = "success" ]; then
    echo "Manifest hashes match every file in \`logos/\`."
  else
    echo "Manifest verification FAILED — \`logos/\` and \`manifest.json\` are out of sync."
  fi
} >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"

commands.step: Install npm >=11.5 in a sandbox for OIDC trusted-publishing auth
commands.text:
# Node 22 ships npm 10.9, which signs provenance but cannot negotiate
# the OIDC auth path (PUT returns a misleading 404). An in-place
# `npm i -g npm@latest` races the bundled arborist and breaks — install
# npm@latest into a sandbox dir and shadow the system npm via PATH.
SANDBOX="$HOME/.npm-cli-sandbox"
mkdir -p "$SANDBOX"
pushd "$SANDBOX" >/dev/null
echo '{"name":"npm-cli-sandbox","version":"0.0.0","private":true}' > package.json
npm install --no-save --no-audit --no-fund --silent npm@latest
popd >/dev/null
echo "$SANDBOX/node_modules/.bin" >> "$GITHUB_PATH"
"$SANDBOX/node_modules/.bin/npm" --version

PKG_VERSION=$(node -p "require('./package.json').version")
TAG_VERSION="${{ steps.tag.outputs.version }}"
echo "Tag: ${{ steps.tag.outputs.tag }} -> ${TAG_VERSION} | package.json: ${PKG_VERSION}"
if [ "${PKG_VERSION}" != "${TAG_VERSION}" ]; then
  echo "::error::Tag ${TAG_VERSION} does not match package.json version ${PKG_VERSION}"
  exit 1
fi

commands.step: Publish to npm with provenance (OIDC trusted publisher, no token)
Extract CHANGELOG section for the release notes
commands.text:
VERSION="${{ steps.tag.outputs.version }}"
awk -v ver="$VERSION" '
  $0 ~ ("^## " ver "( |$)") {flag=1; next}
  flag && /^## / {exit}
  flag {print}
' CHANGELOG.md > release-notes.md
if [ -s release-notes.md ]; then
  echo "have_notes=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
else
  echo "have_notes=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
fi

TAG="${{ steps.tag.outputs.tag }}"
if [ "${{ steps.notes.outputs.have_notes }}" = "true" ]; then
  gh release create "$TAG" --title "brand $TAG" --notes-file release-notes.md --verify-tag
else
  gh release create "$TAG" --title "brand $TAG" --generate-notes --verify-tag
fi

set +e
bash scripts/sync-org-logos.sh
code=$?
set -e
if [ "$code" -eq 10 ]; then
  echo "changed=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
elif [ "$code" -eq 0 ]; then
  echo "changed=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
else
  exit "$code"
fi

git config user.name "github-actions[bot]"
git config user.email "41898282+github-actions[bot]@users.noreply.github.com"
# Stable branch name (not date/run_id-suffixed) so every daily run
# updates the SAME branch instead of minting a new one. Previously
# each run created auto/sync-logos-<date>-<run_id>, which meant a
# brand-new PR every single day the sync found changes — 31+ open
# auto-sync PRs accumulated with nobody merging or closing them.
# `-B` + `push --force-with-lease` below intentionally overwrite the
# branch's prior bot-authored content each run (this also subsumes
# the old run_id suffix's original purpose of avoiding a same-day
# rerun push collision — force-pushing never collides).
#
# Trade-off: this branch is a STABLE, shared name, so it may be the
# head ref of an open, human-reviewed PR. If a reviewer pushes a
# fixup commit directly onto it between scheduled runs, plain
# `--force` would silently discard that commit. `--force-with-lease`
# refuses to push when the remote tip has moved since the fetch
# immediately below, so a human's commit makes THIS run fail loudly
# instead of vanishing quietly. That fetch narrows the race window
# (fetch, then push moments later) but does not close it completely
# — a push landing in that gap is still possible, just far less
# likely than with no fetch at all (the old code never fetched, so
# it always overwrote blind).
BRANCH="auto/sync-logos"
# actions/checkout only fetches the ref that triggered this run
# (main, for schedule/workflow_dispatch) — never this stable side
# branch — so without an explicit fetch here, git has no local
# record of the branch's real remote tip and --force-with-lease
# below would have nothing to compare against. `|| true`: the
# branch may not exist yet on the very first run.
git fetch origin "$BRANCH:refs/remotes/origin/$BRANCH" 2>/dev/null || true
git checkout -B "$BRANCH"
git add logos/ manifest.json
git diff --cached --quiet && { echo 'nothing to commit'; exit 0; }
git commit -m "chore: sync org logos ($(date -u +%Y-%m-%d))"
git push --force-with-lease="$BRANCH" -u origin "$BRANCH"
# `gh pr create` fails hard when the repo setting "Allow GitHub Actions
# to create and approve pull requests" is OFF and no SYNC_PAT is set —
# this used to fail the daily run red AND (under the old per-run
# dated-branch design) leave an orphan branch behind every single
# day. Degrade gracefully instead: warn loudly with the likely
# remediation, leave the already-pushed branch in place (the else
# branch below intentionally no longer deletes it — see its
# comment), and exit 0. Once the setting/secret is in place the same
# step opens PRs normally; until then the run is a clean amber and
# the stable branch is simply reused next time.
PR_BODY=$(cat <<'EOF'
## Auto-sync

Daily logo sync from all repos in **mcp-tool-shop-org**.

- New logos added to `logos/`
- Updated logos replaced
- `manifest.json` regenerated

**Review:** Check the diff for any unexpected additions or hash changes before merging.

**Do not push commits directly to this branch.** The next scheduled
run force-pushes it (via `--force-with-lease`) and will FAIL loudly
if your commit is on top by then, rather than silently overwriting
it — but it also won't merge your fix in. Make manual changes in a
separate branch/PR instead.
EOF
)
# Dedup by branch, mirroring the label-based dedup the "Open issue on
# verify failure" step already does below: an open PR on this stable
# branch was just updated in place by the force-push above, so
# creating another would only duplicate it.
existing=$(gh pr list --state open --head "$BRANCH" --json number --jq 'length')
if [ "${existing:-0}" -gt 0 ]; then
  echo "Open PR already tracks $BRANCH — force-push above updated it in place; not creating a duplicate."
  echo "pr_opened=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
elif gh pr create \
  --title "chore: sync org logos ($(date -u +%Y-%m-%d))" \
  --body "$PR_BODY"; then
  echo "pr_opened=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
else
  # `gh pr create` can fail for reasons other than the permissions
  # gap the warning used to assume: a transient API error, rate
  # limiting, or a race where the dedup check above missed an
  # already-open PR because of search-index lag right after the
  # force-push. This branch is STABLE (auto/sync-logos, reused
  # every run — see the comment above, not a per-run dated branch),
  # so it may be the head ref of a currently-open, possibly
  # human-reviewed PR. It is intentionally left in place — deleting
  # it here could sever that PR's head ref, and under the
  # stable-branch design a delete buys no cruft-avoidance benefit
  # anyway (the next run's checkout -B + force-push recreates or
  # overwrites it unconditionally regardless of whether it exists).
  # The commit was already force-pushed above either way, so
  # nothing is lost by leaving the branch as-is.
  echo "::warning title=Sync PR not opened::gh pr create failed. This may mean 'Allow GitHub Actions to create and approve pull requests' is OFF and no SYNC_PAT is set (Settings -> Actions -> General), or it may be a transient error (API/rate-limit/index-lag). Branch $BRANCH was force-pushed and left in place -- open the PR manually if needed, or re-run this workflow."
  echo "pr_opened=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
fi

ADDED="${{ steps.sync.outputs.added }}"
CHANGED_COUNT="${{ steps.sync.outputs.changed_count }}"
UNCHANGED="${{ steps.sync.outputs.unchanged }}"
SKIPPED="${{ steps.sync.outputs.skipped }}"
REJECTED="${{ steps.sync.outputs.rejected }}"
NET_ERR="${{ steps.sync.outputs.network_errors }}"
SUSPICIOUS_COUNT="${{ steps.sync.outputs.suspicious_count }}"
{
  echo "## Daily sync — $(date -u +%Y-%m-%d)"
  echo ""
  echo "| Metric | Count |"
  echo "| --- | --- |"
  echo "| New logos | ${ADDED:-0} |"
  echo "| Updated logos | ${CHANGED_COUNT:-0} |"
  echo "| Unchanged | ${UNCHANGED:-0} |"
  echo "| No logo found | ${SKIPPED:-0} |"
  echo "| Rejected (not an image / too large) | ${REJECTED:-0} |"
  echo "| Network errors | ${NET_ERR:-0} |"
  echo "| Suspicious divergence | ${SUSPICIOUS_COUNT:-0} |"
  echo ""
  echo "Repo changes detected: ${{ steps.sync.outputs.changed }}"
  if [ "${{ steps.verify.outcome }}" = "failure" ]; then
    echo ""
    echo "Manifest verification FAILED — see the Verify regenerated manifest step."
  fi
  if [ -n "${SUSPICIOUS_COUNT:-}" ] && [ "${SUSPICIOUS_COUNT:-0}" != "0" ]; then
    echo ""
    echo "### Suspicious logo divergence"
    echo ""
    echo "The registry's copy differed from upstream for the logo(s) below, AND"
    echo "the most recent commit to touch that file in this repo's history was"
    echo "NOT the sync automation's own commit. This does not by itself prove"
    echo "tampering -- git commit authorship is self-reported and this repo does"
    echo "not require signed commits (see \`.github/SECURITY-CONTROLS.md\`) -- but"
    echo "it is not explained by a normal sync cycle either. Tracked via a"
    echo "labelled issue (\`logo-divergence-suspicious\`) so it isn't only visible"
    echo "in this run's summary."
    echo ""
    echo '```'
    echo "$SUSPICIOUS_DETAILS"
    echo '```'
  fi
} >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"

commands.step: Open issue on suspicious logo divergence
commands.text:
existing=$(gh issue list --label logo-divergence-suspicious --state open --json number --jq 'length')
if [ "${existing:-0}" -gt 0 ]; then
  echo "An open logo-divergence-suspicious issue already exists — not opening another."
  exit 0
fi
# Idempotent: creates the label the first time this ever fires,
# updates its color/description in place on later runs, and never
# errors just because the label already exists.
gh label create logo-divergence-suspicious \
  --color B60205 \
  --description "Sync tripwire: registry logo diverged from upstream outside the normal sync flow" \
  --force >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
{
  echo "The daily logo sync found **$SUSPICIOUS_COUNT** logo(s) where the"
  echo "registry's copy differed from upstream AND the most recent commit to"
  echo "touch that file in this repo's history was not the sync automation's"
  echo "own commit."
  echo ""
  echo "Affected:"
  echo '```'
  echo "$SUSPICIOUS_DETAILS"
  echo '```'
  echo ""
  echo "This does not by itself prove tampering — git commit authorship is"
  echo "self-reported and this repo does not currently require signed commits"
  echo "(see \`.github/SECURITY-CONTROLS.md\`). It means a human should confirm"
  echo "who made that commit and why before assuming it's benign."
  echo ""
  echo "The sync PR proceeds normally for review; this issue exists so the"
  echo "anomaly itself is tracked and not lost in an Actions log nobody reads."
  echo ""
  echo "See [run log]($RUN_URL)."
} > /tmp/suspicious-issue-body.md
gh issue create \
  --title "Suspicious logo divergence detected ($(date -u +%Y-%m-%d))" \
  --label logo-divergence-suspicious \
  --body-file /tmp/suspicious-issue-body.md

existing=$(gh issue list --label sync-failure --state open --json number --jq 'length')
if [ "${existing:-0}" -gt 0 ]; then
  echo "An open sync-failure issue already exists — not opening another."
  exit 0
fi
RUN_URL="${{ github.server_url }}/${{ github.repository }}/actions/runs/${{ github.run_id }}"
gh issue create \
  --title "Daily sync: manifest verify failed ($(date -u +%Y-%m-%d))" \
  --label sync-failure \
  --body "The daily sync regenerated \`manifest.json\` but verification failed. See [run log]($RUN_URL)."
